description: Lifesaving teaches you to help someone in trouble in the water while keeping yourself safe — starting with reaching, throwing and rowing rescues and moving to carefully supervised in-water rescues, escapes, spinal injury management and CPR.

safety.note: Water rescue skills must be learned and practiced only with a qualified aquatics instructor and Safe Swim Defense in place. Never attempt an in-water rescue you have not been trained for.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Excerpts confirmed requirements 1, 4 and 5 and the prerequisite swimming items; requirements 6 onward (rowing and in-water rescues, escapes, submerged-victim recovery, spinal injury management, CPR and other injuries) were not visible with their numbers and are not outlined yet.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safe Swim Defense
requirements.summary: Reviewing the principles of Safe Swim Defense with your counselor before the in-water requirements.

requirements.title: Prerequisites
requirements.summary: Earning the Swimming merit badge before the in-water requirements.

requirements.title: Endurance swim
requirements.summary: A strong continuous swim using several strokes, as described in the official requirement.

requirements.title: Reaching rescues
requirements.summary: Demonstrating reaching rescues with everyday items such as arms, legs, towels, paddles or poles.

requirements.title: Throwing rescues
requirements.summary: Demonstrating throwing rescues with a line, ring buoy, rescue bag or other floating support.
